draft.title: Families of organic compounds
card: Organic compounds are built on chains of carbon atoms. A family is a group of compounds that share a general formula and a similar set of properties.
These contain only carbon and hydrogen. Alkanes have only single bonds between carbons (CnH2n+2). Alkenes have one C=C double bond (CnH2n).
These are alkanes where one or more hydrogen atoms are replaced by a halogen atom, such as chlorine or bromine.
Alcohols (CnH2n+1OH) contain an OH group. Carboxylic acids (CnH2n+1COOH) contain a COOH group and act as weak acids.
draft.remember: Each family has a general formula, and its group of atoms gives its properties.

a.q: Which compound is an alkene, using its general formula?
a.why: Alkenes follow CnH2n, and C3H6 fits with n = 3. C3H8 is tempting because it has only carbon and hydrogen, but it fits CnH2n+2, so it is an alkane.

b.q: A lab technician has a liquid with the formula C2H5Br. Which family does it belong to?
b.why: One hydrogen of ethane has been replaced by a bromine atom, so it is a haloalkane. It is not an alkane, because an alkane has only carbon and hydrogen atoms.
b.clue: Look for an atom other than carbon and hydrogen.
